title: CW-Lite Clock Glitch Configuration for MX Coprocessor FI
status: WORKING — produces crashes and persistent FPGA configuration faults

hardware.fpga_design: CROC SoC (CVE2 + MX Unified Coprocessor via CVXIF)
hardware.firmware: qnn_llm_mxint8 (2-layer GPT decoder, MXINT8 dot products)
hardware.connection: 20-pin ribbon cable (standard, no jumper wires needed)
hardware.sma_x3: Not used for clock glitch (crowbar, disconnected OK)
hardware.sma_x4: Not used for clock glitch (measure, disconnected OK)

dip_switches.J16_note: Clock source = CW-Lite HS2 (glitched clock via BUFGMUX)

trigger_mechanism.type: USB register (usb_clk domain, no soc_clk dependency)
sequence: 3. time.sleep(0.001)                — let firmware reach target region
5. target.fpga_write(0x05, [0x01])  — USB trigger HIGH → glitch fires

persistent_config_fault.effect: FPGA SRAM bit-flip, ret=27 (golden=25), XOR=0x2, 1 bit flipped
persistent_config_fault.note: Persistent — same wrong result until FPGA reprogrammed

husky_note: Husky does NOT work with this CW305 — HS2 pin routing differs. CW-Lite's DCM-based glitch module routes clock_xor to HS2 which reaches CW305 N14 via the 20-pin cable. Husky's PLL-based module does not.
